sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None turned up on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.

2. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant aged about 15 years was enticed by the applicant, subsequently, in the statement under Section 1611 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she had gone along with the applicant to Ludhiana, where they stayed for about 2-1/2 months and the in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C, the victim disclosed her age as 17 years and stated that she was in love with the applicant and had gone along with him.

sentences.text: 3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.
4. Considering the two statements not supporting the prosecution story, the applicnat who is custody since 14.07.2023 is enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Ram Niwas be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 106 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 5 Tha/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Sirsiya, District Shrawasti, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
